newsitem.title: USA: Interstate Bakeries price rise offsets costs.
newsitem.headline: Interstate Bakeries price rise offsets costs.

text.p: Interstate Bakeries Corp, the largest U.S. baker and distributor of fresh branded bread and cake products, said Thursday price increases helped it offset higher ingredient costs.

While escalating ingredient prices were a concern in its fiscal first quarter ended August 24, recent trends in the commodity markets indicate the worst may be over, Charles Sullivan, chairman, said in a statement.
"Though we have little control over commodity prices, as a major food company we are capable of taking appropriate action to protect our profit margins," he added.
Earlier, Interstate Bakeries reported first quarter earnings of $0.49 a share, up from $0.21 a year ago.
"Despite more than doubling our size, we remain agile, are utilizing our economies of scale and are continuing our efforts toward keeping costs in line," Sullivan said.
Interstate Bakeries acquired Continental Baking from Ralston Purina Co in July 1995.
Sullivan also said the company's brand-building efforts were on target.
